findings.F1: The scaled-fall rebound grows with the agitation of the coin's current swing, whatever the trend. On days with a fall of more than one 30-day standard deviation, the next day's excess return is +1.77 % (t 4.69, 232 cases) when the coin's 30-day swing ranks in the upper third of its recent swings. It is +0.60 % (t 1.52, 236 cases) in the middle third and -0.22 % (t -0.59, 167 cases) in the lower third, across all trends.

findings.F3: In the falling agitated profile, the bounce does not fade after the first day. After falls beyond one standard deviation (129 cases), the mean return is +2.91 % over the next day (t 4.46), +2.51 % over two days (t 3.26) and +3.57 % over three days (t 3.84). These are overlapping returns from distinct signal bars, not a non-overlapping grid.

ideas.idea: In an agitated market, the larger a coin's one-day fall against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the last 30 days, the larger its rise over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader can buy outsized falls whenever the coin is swinging more than usual, not only in declines, and refuse the same trade when the coin is calm.
ideas.name: agitated outsized fall rebounds

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, the larger a coin's one-day fall against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the last 30 days, the larger its rise over the next three days.
ideas.consequence: The rebound after a forced sweep in an agitated decline keeps building for several days, so a trader can hold it longer than one day and pay the trade's cost once for a larger move.
ideas.name: agitated fall three-day rebound
